ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Preventive Visit — Paul Robeson — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Mr. Robeson is a 59-year-old singer and actor with recurrent major depression who comes for the preventive visit booked in the spring. Six weeks ago aripiprazole was added to venlafaxine 225 mg; he has taken 5 mg each morning for four weeks. He sleeps about six and a half hours, his energy and interest have come back, and he practices every morning and sang at two community gatherings last month. He has noticed no restlessness, stiffness or tremor; his weight is up 1.4 kg in six weeks. The cough from the summer cleared within three weeks. He continues weekly behavioral activation and is planning a small recital. He has had no thoughts of suicide. [S]

Sustained political persecution: passport withheld, concerts and recordings cancelled, income lost, and surveillance by federal agencies; a major and realistic stressor, not a delusion
S — Synthetic coding of his documented persecution as a social determinant of his depression.

S — Synthetic intercurrent illness; not a historical claim.

Follow-up: Mood review with weight in two weeks, at eight weeks of aripiprazole; twelve-week metabolic tests. FIT result and screening results by phone. Second zoster dose in two to six months. Call or text 988 at any time in a crisis. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with his consent. He wants full treatment of any illness. He named a health care agent, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here. He asked that any future decision about ECT be his own, made with his own informed consent while he has capacity; this was recorded as his stated preference. To be revisited yearly. [S]
